strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across three modalities (NMR, X-ray crystallography, protein-protein interactions) with substantial benchmarks (20 NMR proteins, 13 X-ray structures, 7 complexes) showing consistent improvements over strong baselines

Important novel finding that ipTM confidence scores can be artificially inflated via small embedding perturbations (0.01%), with thorough analysis using complementary metrics (DockQ, Fnat, ipSAE, H-bond recovery)
Rigorous mathematical framework with formal convergence analysis (Theorem B.8) providing O(1/K) guarantees and careful treatment of bias sources (Lemmas B.1, B.5, B.6)
Principled energy-weighted Boltzmann sampling for thermodynamic consistency, with careful numerical treatment (temperature annealing, energy smoothing)
Exceptional reproducibility support including detailed pseudocode, hyperparameter justification via ablation studies (Tables 8-9), and implementation details for differentiable operations
Model-agnostic framework demonstrated across multiple models (AF3, Protenix, Boltz-2), indicating broad applicability
Reduced run-to-run variability compared to coordinate-space guidance (Figure 15), indicating more stable optimization
weaknesses: Key theoretical assumptions (local Lipschitz smoothness, Jensen's inequality tightness, bias impact from dropped REINFORCE term) lack empirical validation, limiting confidence in theoretical guarantees
Significant computational overhead: 10-15% higher GPU memory and ~1.1-1.2x longer wall-clock time per loop than coordinate-space guidance, with practical advantage depending on available resources

Mixed ipTM guidance results on small benchmark (7 complexes): improves only 2/7 cases substantially; paper documents vulnerability but provides minimal actionable mitigation beyond 'interpret cautiously'

Energy model dependency under-explored: Boltzmann reweighting relies entirely on ProteinEBM; robustness to alternative force fields (AMBER, CHARMM, Rosetta) not evaluated despite NMR relaxation using AMBER99SB
Hyperparameter choices insufficiently justified: learning rate, outer iterations, ensemble size, and annealing breakpoints lack principled selection or sensitivity analysis beyond Table 8
Limited experimental scope: X-ray experiments restricted to single chains, cryo-EM not evaluated despite motivation, no evaluation on protein-small molecule complexes
Baseline comparison limitations: primary baseline (Maddipatla et al. 2025a) from overlapping authorship; inconsistent improvements (Figure 4D shows ~3-5% median violation reduction, which is modest)
Incomplete ablations: no analysis of ensemble size scaling (n=16 fixed), MSA quality robustness, or failure mode characterization; use of Protenix vs. official AF3 may affect reproducibility

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple modalities (NMR, X-ray crystallography, ipTM) with 40+ structures/complexes, multiple baselines, and extensive ablations
Important and novel finding that ipTM confidence metrics can be artificially inflated through tiny embedding perturbations (0.01%), with implications for protein design workflows
Technically sound approach with principled use of ELBO, Boltzmann reweighting, and convergence analysis in appendices
Demonstrated generalization across different protein generative models (AF3, Boltz-2), suggesting broader applicability
Excellent supplementary material with detailed implementation details, hyperparameter justification, and theoretical analysis
Clear presentation of the core methodological difference between embedding-space and coordinate-space guidance (Figures 1-3)
weaknesses: Critical flaw: At equivalent computational budgets (Table 20), IT-Opt provides only marginal improvements over standard guidance, sometimes underperforming. This undermines the efficiency claims and suggests improvements stem from increased compute rather than better methodology

Limited methodological novelty: embedding-space vs. coordinate-space optimization is a straightforward engineering choice; ELBO and Boltzmann reweighting are standard techniques applied competently but not innovatively

Substantial theory-practice gap: actual optimization (Eq. 2 + many heuristics) differs significantly from theoretical target (Eq. 1), with unquantified ELBO bound tightness and biased gradient estimators (Lemma B.1) receiving minimal main-text discussion

Excessive method complexity with numerous hyperparameters (learning rate, clipping, loop iterations, prior weight, validity weights, energy annealing, EMA smoothing, percentile biasing, etc.) and modality-specific tuning (different settings for NMR vs. ipTM) with limited principled guidance for practitioners

Selective benchmarking with cherry-picked examples: X-ray results emphasize two hand-selected cases (3AZY:A, 6I42:B); ipTM results mixed with many cases showing no structural improvement despite confidence gains (Figures 7, 10); limited failure case analysis

Overfitting concerns underexplored: method often fits better than deposited PDB structures, raising questions about whether ensembles represent artifacts/noise in experimental data rather than biological reality

Energy reweighting provides marginal benefits: sometimes helps, sometimes hurts (Table 4); effective sample size often no better than unweighted (Table 7); implementation requires many heuristics suggesting numerical instability rather than principled solutions
ipTM analysis, while novel, feels orthogonal to main IT-Opt narrative; it exposes an AF3 limitation rather than demonstrating IT-Opt superiority, and improvements are inconsistent across targets

Statistical rigor concerns: most results lack error bars or significance testing; reproducibility across random seeds unclear for NMR/ipTM; limited seed-to-seed variability analysis outside crystallography (Figure 15)
Theory-practice gap on Gaussian prior: p(Z|a) = N(Z(a), σ²) seems overly restrictive for embedding manifold and is not well motivated; sensitivity to prior variance σ² not explored

strengths: Well-motivated representation-space optimization framework that elegantly addresses limitations of coordinate-space guidance by maintaining embedding updates across diffusion iterations
Rigorous theoretical analysis with formal convergence guarantees (Theorem B.8) and explicit bias/variance characterization (Lemmas B.4-B.6)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three complementary modalities (NMR, X-ray crystallography, protein complexes) with consistent improvements over strong baselines
Principled Boltzmann reweighting approach that bridges ML predictions with thermodynamic priors using self-normalized importance sampling
Important practical finding that ipTM confidence scores can be artificially inflated through minimal embedding perturbations without structural improvement, with implications for binder engineering
Extensive supplementary material with hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Table 8), compute-normalized comparisons (Table 20), and multiple ablations demonstrating robustness
Results frequently exceed PDB-deposited structures (Figure 4) with improved reproducibility across random seeds (Figure 15)
weaknesses: Reproducibility concerns due to use of Protenix (open-source reimplementation) instead of official AF3 for most experiments, making it difficult to isolate whether improvements stem from the method or Protenix-specific behavior

Theoretical analysis establishes convergence to a near-stationary region with bounds dependent on difficult-to-quantify terms (Fisher information trace, Lipschitz constants); convergence rate is loose and may not be tight in practice
Non-negligible computational overhead (~14% slower than Guidance per iteration, Table 19) with modest improvements (5-10% across most metrics), raising questions about practical cost-benefit tradeoff

Limited scope of ipTM experiments (only 7 complexes) with high variability across targets and inconsistent improvements, suggesting limited effectiveness of confidence-driven optimization for design applications
X-ray benchmarks restricted to short sequence segments (6-20 residues for peptides, 7 residues for altlocs); unclear if IT-Opt scales to full proteins
Heavy dependency on ProteinEBM energy model for Boltzmann reweighting with limited exploration of alternative energy models; energy model accuracy fundamentally limits thermodynamic consistency
Many hyperparameter choices (validity loss weights, energy annealing schedules, stopping points) only validated on single proteins; generalizability across diverse protein systems unclear
Incomplete ablation studies: unclear how much improvement comes from core IT-Optimization vs. validity likelihood regularization terms vs. energy-based reweighting
